learning: Forward offset 0.06 m gave the best total score so far, but it moved the s-bend progress down. If the next race shows the same s-bend loss point and steering oscillation below about 0.2, the next offset to test is 0.055 m. If oscillation rises above 0.2, the forward offset has reached its useful limit.
notes: Complete runnable package: the iteration 9 design (best measured, 52.985) with its paired controller held fixed. Only the geometry is the Builder's iteration 10 proposal, which matches iteration 9 exactly, so this run is a repeat that confirms the offset result and gives a clean per-track readout. All values are inside the contract limits.
rationale: Iteration 9 is the best measured design at 52.985. Moving the five 12 mm sensors from y 0.05 to y 0.06 m raised oval progress from 0.138 to 0.151 (oval score 56.25 to 62.77) and lowered s-bend progress from 0.148 to 0.140 (s-bend score 61.01 to 57.74). Slalom progress held at 0.097. Line loss stayed at 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend and at 2.0 on slalom, and steering oscillation stayed low (0.10 and 0.14). The robot is therefore not jittering, and the loss is a single dropout at a fixed point. Iteration 9 is the only run that changed sensing and kept the controller, so the controller pairing is already known to work with this layout. I keep the iteration 9 controller unchanged (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.6, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], last_direction). Changing the controller in the same run would add an untested variable, and the Builder's question (is the s-bend loss at the same progress point?) needs a clean geometry readout. Geometry is exactly the Builder's proposal: five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.06 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, body unchanged. I expect a score near 52.9 to 53.0, with the single line loss still present on oval and s-bend.
